column2: req_desc

Run manifest and health check
/app/run.json installs, builds and serves the app on port 4173 (or APP_PUBLIC_PORT), and GET /api/health answers 200 {"status":"ok"} even while MinIO or the game server is unreachable.

Security headers on every response
Every response carries the content security policy, transport, sniffing, framing and referrer headers listed under Server boundary, with a fresh script nonce each time.

Developer and moderator sign-in
Signing in with a seeded email and password sets HttpOnly SameSite=Strict session cookies and returns the session's change token, and wrong credentials get the published 401.

Short access tokens with revocation
Access tokens expire after ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS (600 by default), and a token revoked at sign-out answers 401 at once.

Rotating refresh-token families
Each refresh rotates the refresh token, and presenting a superseded one revokes the whole family with no grace window, as qualified in Business rules.

Signed widget identity
Widget requests are honoured only with a player id signed under the game's widget secret, and without a valid signature there is no thread to read or write.

Player starts and reopens a thread
A player's first message from the widget opens a waiting thread with the chosen topic, and a later new message moves an answered or closed thread back to waiting, while a replayed send changes nothing.

Players see only their own thread
A player who sends another player's thread, message or attachment id gets the same 404 as for an id that does not exist.

Player text renders inert
Player text is stored as submitted and shown through the formatting allowlist in the inbox, the widget and Tamperglass, never running a script or carrying a link outside the allowlist.

Phone widget works by touch
At 375 by 812 with touch input, a player picks a topic, writes, attaches a file and sends using taps alone, on targets at least 44 px in each direction.

Per-player token bucket
Each player's sends draw on their own eight-token bucket held in Postgres that refills one token every 15 seconds, an empty bucket answers 429 with Retry-After unless the send replays an earlier success, and concurrent sends never overdraw it.

Rate-limit notice in the widget
A send refused by the bucket shows and announces the published rate-limit notice with the server's Retry-After seconds and disables Send.

Attachment upload limits
A player attaches up to three files of 1 to 5,000,000 bytes each to their own message, and anything else is refused with its published status.

Attached only after the store confirms
An attachment reads uploading until MinIO confirms the stored object, then attached, or failed if the store refuses it.

Attachments served only through Hushline
Attachment bytes come only through Hushline's own authorised routes, to the owning player or to staff of the owning game, under a sandboxed content policy, never from a bucket address.

Signed game-server events
Game-server events are accepted only with a valid signature over timestamp and body, inside the 300-second window and with an unused nonce, and each refusal answers its published status.

One purchase per receipt
A receipt id becomes at most one purchase and a refund id at most one refund, even when sent again with fresh nonces, with a different amount or concurrently, and the original always wins.

Refused events stay on the record
A refused event naming a known player appears in that player's thread for staff as a refused entry, never as a purchase or refund, and is announced in the open workspace.

Formatting allowlist and sanitiser record
Each player message's sanitiser stage records the text before, the text after and every removed span, by the published removal rules.

Link previews from public addresses only
The first web link in a player message is previewed only from a public address the fetch was pinned to, and loopback, private, link-local, shared, metadata and reserved targets are refused with their class.

Redirects rechecked and fetches capped
Every redirect is checked again like a new link, at most three are followed, and a fetch stops at 524,288 bytes or 3 seconds.

Inbox by status with permitted counts
The inbox lists the caller's game's threads by status in pages, with counts and search that include only threads the caller may read.

Empty inbox copy
A status tab or search with no threads shows the published empty-state sentence.

Thread view with purchases and events
Opening a thread shows its player messages, replies, events, attachments, link previews and purchase list with refunded amounts, in time order.

Developers stay inside their own game
Any thread, message, attachment, forensics or moderator id that belongs to another game answers the same 404 as an unknown id.

Verdicts computed once and stored
Each message's verdicts are computed when it is received, stored, and read back unchanged from the forensics endpoint and its stream.

Change token on every staff action
Every staff state change, including reply, close, rule grant and rule revoke, is refused with 403 without the session's change token or with a foreign Origin.

Reply to a player
A reply moves a waiting thread to answered, is refused on a closed thread unless it replays an earlier successful reply, and appears in the player's widget within five seconds.

Close and reopen threads
Only an answered thread can be closed, exactly one of two simultaneous closes succeeds, and each illegal close gets its published 409.

Reply and close announcements
Sending a reply and closing a thread are announced in the workspace live region with the published pending, success and failure copy.

Game-server receipt lookup
Opening a thread asks the game server afresh for the player's receipts and shows its record beside the signed purchases.

Honest lookup outage and recovery
When the game server does not answer, the thread shows the published outage copy and keeps working, and the next lookup after the server returns succeeds without a restart.

Moderator grants and denies
The developer adds and revokes grant and deny rules for each moderator by action and topic, and each change applies from the moderator's very next request.

Deny overrides every surface
An explicit deny beats any grant on every route and derived surface, including inbox counts, pages, search, thread view, forensics, attachments, lookups and live updates.

Keyboard-complete inbox
The developer moves between threads, steps through messages with Tamperglass following, replies, closes, and opens and dismisses panes with the published keys, whichever workspace control has focus, and the keys are held back while a drawer or sheet is open.

Published breakpoints
The workspace shows three panes at 1280 by 800, thread plus Tamperglass at 768 by 1024, and a single thread with Tamperglass as a sheet at 375 by 812, with no horizontal overflow.

Closed sheet and drawer are inert
A closed Tamperglass sheet or thread drawer is hidden, out of the tab order and absent from the accessibility tree at every viewport.

Tamperglass streams four lines
Selecting a message shows four lines in a fixed order that read checking and each settle as its stage arrives, ending exactly as the stored forensics read, and a stream for an earlier selection never writes into them.

Settle and fill motion
Each line settles from checking to its verdict in about a sixth of a second, and the bucket fill moves from the previous level to the new one in about a quarter of a second, with no looping motion anywhere.

Reduced-motion Tamperglass
Under reduced motion every line switches to its verdict and the bucket fill jumps to its level with no transition, and sheets and drawers open without sliding.

Verdicts announced once settled
Once all four lines for the selected message have settled, the Verdicts live region announces them once in the published sentence.

Not-found page
Any unknown page answers 404 and shows the published not-found sentence with a link back to the inbox.

Public page and hero
The public page carries the quiet-instrument look: stone ground, the surface panel with the blue glass slab on its seam, the italic two-line headline and one accent button.

Workspace visual language
The workspace and widget keep the one left edge, EB Garamond, two inks, square corners, word statuses and one accent element per screen, with hostile text quoted as italic evidence.

Credentials from the environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment at start, never hard-coded and never sent to the browser.

Retried replies store one message
The same Idempotency-Key on a reply stores one message and replays the original 201, also after the thread closed, as qualified in Business rules.

Expired session resumes the reply
When the access token expires mid-reply the workspace makes exactly one refresh and sends the reply once, and when the session has ended sign-in returns to the same thread with the unsent text restored.

Retried widget sends store one message
The same Idempotency-Key on a widget send stores one message and replays the original 201, also after the player's bucket emptied, as qualified in Business rules.

Rate-limit state comes from the server
The widget shows the rate-limit notice and a disabled Send whenever the server's latest answer says the bucket is empty, also after a reload or with a wrong device clock, until the server reports a token.

Stable, permission-filled inbox pages
Inbox pages follow opaque cursors that never repeat or skip a thread that keeps its place, and every page but the last is filled with threads the caller may read.

Live rows move in place
A player's new message moves or inserts that thread's row and updates the counts within two seconds without a reload, with focus kept on the same row.

Latest thread wins
A late receipt lookup, Tamperglass stream or search answer never changes what the workspace shows for a newer thread, selection or query, even across closing and reopening the Tamperglass sheet.

Purchases compared with the game server
Each signed purchase is compared field by field with the game server's receipt of the same id, and the differing fields are listed and shown.

Amounts in each currency's minor unit
Purchase and refund amounts are whole minor units in a published currency, shown with exactly that currency's decimals and no grouping.

Drafts survive live updates
A live update or widget refresh never clears a typed message or reply, the chosen topic, picked files, the selected message, an open sheet or drawer, focus or the last announcement.

Declared type must match the bytes
An upload is classified from its bytes as PNG, JPEG or UTF-8 text, refused with 422 unless the declared type equals the detected one, and stored and served as the detected type.

Stored filenames are safe to send back
Each attachment's stored filename has paths, control characters and double quotes removed and is cut to 120 units, and downloads name it in an attachment header with an ASCII fallback and a UTF-8 form.

Partial refunds form one exact ledger
Each purchase's refunded amount is the sum of its accepted refunds in its own currency, capped at the amount, whatever order receipts and refunds arrive in, and reads paid, partly refunded or refunded, as qualified in Business rules.

Rule changes reach open workspaces
Within two seconds of a rule change, the moderator's open workspace and streams drop newly hidden threads from rows, counts, the open thread and stream frames and show newly readable ones, without a reload.

Tab and search live in the URL
The status tab and search are held in the inbox URL, so a reload, Back or a shared link shows the same tab, search and rows.

Streams hold no connection each
Hushline uses at most 10 Postgres connections named hushline, open streams hold none each, a stream whose client leaves stops its work within five seconds, and with 60 streams open a widget send answers and reaches the streams within two seconds.

Landing after close and sign-out
After a close the workspace opens the next loaded row with focus on its heading, and sign-out lands on /signin with the published copy.

Thread statistics count only what happened
Every staff thread body carries `statistics`, whose counters and times move only with a stored message or a successful close, never with a replay, a refused request or an event.

Waiting since the first unanswered message
Inbox rows and the staff thread body carry `waiting_since`, the time of the player message that put the thread into `waiting`, unchanged by later player messages, replays and events, and `null` outside `waiting`.

Server secret rotation with one overlap
The developer replaces the game's server secret, the replaced secret keeps verifying events for `SECRET_OVERLAP_SECONDS`, only one previous secret is ever kept, and events verified with it say so in their signature verdict.

Paged game-server receipts
A receipt lookup follows the game server's `next_cursor` across at most five pages and is either the whole record or unavailable, never a partial one.

Effective permissions with the deciding rules
The developer reads each moderator's effective permission for every action and topic, together with the ids of the rules that decided it, computed by the one deny-over-grant decision.
/app/run.json is valid JSON with string install, build and serve and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and it is the only way the app is installed, built and started.
/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists every shipped package with its version and licence, plus EB Garamond; shipped packages are the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json.
Every shipped package and bundled font is under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, CC0-1.0, BlueOak-1.0.0 or OFL-1.1.

No datastore or cache beyond Postgres and MinIO is used: no Redis, no SQLite, no in-memory store standing in for records, buckets, nonces, idempotency keys or the refund ledger, and no files used as a database.
The provided service definitions and the baseline game-server and web responses are left unmodified.
tsconfig.json sets "strict": true, and no application source is plain JavaScript.
A committed package-lock.json sits at /app, and install uses it.
